segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twenty-Seven. If a transversal cutting two lines makes the alternate interior angles equal, the lines are parallel. Let segment E F fall on segments A B and C D so that the alternate interior angles A E F and E F D are equal. We prove that segment A B is parallel to segment C D.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twenty-Seven. If a transversal cutting two lines makes the alternate interior angles equal, the lines are parallel. Let segment E F fall on segments A B and C D so that the alternate interior angles A E F and E F D are equal. We prove that segment A B is parallel to segment C D.

segments.text: Suppose segment A B is not parallel to segment C D. Then when extended in both directions, they must meet either toward B and D, or toward A and C. Let them be extended and meet toward B and D at point G, forming triangle G E F.

subsegments.text: Suppose segment A B is not parallel to segment C D. Then when extended in both directions, they must meet either toward B and D, or toward A and C. Let them be extended and meet toward B and D at point G, forming triangle G E F.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: In triangle G E F, angle A E F is an exterior angle, and angle E F G is the opposite interior angle. By hypothesis, angle A E F equals angle E F G. Yet by Proposition Sixteen, the exterior angle of a triangle is strictly greater than either opposite interior angle, which is impossible. Thus segments A B and C D cannot meet toward B and D, nor similarly toward A and C. By Definition Twenty-Three, lines in the same plane that never meet in either direction are parallel. Therefore segment A B is parallel to segment C D, as was required to prove.
